prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has knee injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1267; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement is regarding the rear-end collision you were involved in on a street in Pasadena, Texas. Do you understand that this call is being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Please state your full name and the best phone number to reach you.

A: [Claimant name] and I can be reached at [phone number].

Q: Can you describe what you were doing right before the collision?

A: I was driving home from work. Traffic had slowed down ahead of me, so I came to a stop at a light. I was stopped for maybe five or six seconds when I felt the impact from behind.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before it hit you?

A: No, I didn't. I was looking at the light and my mirror was not showing anything unusual. The first thing I noticed was the jolt and my head snapping back.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was.

Q: Did you go to a doctor or emergency room after the accident?

A: I went to an urgent care clinic later that evening. My knee had started swelling and I could barely bend it. They took X-rays and told me to follow up with an orthopedic specialist.

Q: Can you describe your knee injury and how it is affecting you now?

A: My right knee is still swollen and sore. Going up stairs is painful, and I have been using a brace. I've had to take time off from my job because standing for long periods makes it worse.

Q: Have you had any prior injuries or treatment to that same knee?

A: No, not that I can recall. I had no problems with it before this accident.

Q: Is there anything else you would like to add to your statement?

A: No, I think that covers it. I am still waiting to see the specialist and I'm hoping to get it sorted out.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
